about.text: a sour milk cheese made in and named after Nieheim, a town in Höxter district in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

sources.text: PGI since 13 May 2010. Soured milk heated to 50 C, curd dried in a bag, ground, ripened warm by its own bacteria and yeasts with no added cultures; salted, often caraway; sliceable (45-46% dry matter) or hard grating form; under 1% fat; small 32-37 g cheeses, sometimes covered in hop leaves
